topics.label: Lecture opening and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students, connects the session to histopathology practicals, and outlines the learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Tumor virology, cellular oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and the experimental assays used to measure cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and functional mechanisms of cancer gene mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the concepts and genetic mechanisms distinguishing oncogenes from tumor suppressor genes through cell cycle regulators and gene dosage effects.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how defects in DNA repair pathways, replication fidelity, and mitotic chromosome segregation cause sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-step acquisition of mutations during tumor development and how inherited germline mutations accelerate this progression.

topics.label: Closing remarks and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a book recommendation and previews the next lecture on cancer hallmarks.
